q: How do I calculate the emissions of one batch in a chemical reactor?
title: Batch reactor emissions per batch
short: Add the steam the reactor took for heating, as a share of boiler fuel, the electricity for the agitator and brine chilling at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, and any thermic fluid heating. Divide by the batch output in kilograms, and keep the batch record as evidence.
audience: Specialty chemical, dye intermediate and API manufacturers

ul: Steam or thermic fluid for heating and distillation.
Chilled brine or cooling water for exothermic steps.
Agitator, vacuum pump and transfer pump power.

p: The batch manufacturing record can give start and end times, steam valve hours and yield. Meter readings beat design values; label design values as estimates.
Divide by the dry weight of good output. Rework batches add energy without adding output, so they raise the per-kilogram figure and belong in it.

example.title: Worked example: one batch (illustrative inputs)
lines: Boiler PNG: 6,000 scm x 2.05 = 12,300 kg CO2 for 80 t steam
Reactor R-3 heating: 9 t steam of 80 = 11.2%
Reactor agitator and chilled brine: 1,100 kWh x 0.710 = 781 kg CO2
Per batch: 2,164.8 kg CO2; batch output 2,400 kg, so 0.902 kg CO2 per kg
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use steam meter readings and the batch manufacturing record.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 records. A per-unit figure divides those by the output you enter, and purchased materials are added from supplier data on the Scope 3 trail, labelled by source.
